Scoring & Playmaking

Volume, Vision, and True Shooting Efficiency Across All 5,160 NBA Players

A common myth about LeBron James is that he is “actually a pass-first player, not a natural scorer” — or conversely, that he broke Kareem Abdul-Jabbar’s scoring record simply by playing a lot of games. Plotting all 5,160 players in NBA history exposes why both myths fall apart: LeBron combines #1 all-time scoring volume with top-4 point-guard playmaking and superior shooting efficiency.

1. Every NBA Player in History: Career Points vs. Assists

Every dot below is a real NBA career. Pure point guards like John Stockton and Chris Paul sit high on the vertical axis (assists) with under 25,000 points. Pure scorers like Michael Jordan, Kobe Bryant, Wilt Chamberlain, and Karl Malone push past 30,000 points on the horizontal axis with roughly half of LeBron’s assists.

Interactive tip: Click any scoring tier in the legend to hide or isolate groups, or drag a box to zoom into any cluster of players.

2. Efficiency Check: Did LeBron Just Shoot More?

To test efficiency fairly across two-pointers, three-pointers, and free throws, basketball analysts use True Shooting Percentage (TS%):

\[\text{TS\%} = \frac{\text{Points}}{2 \times (\text{FGA} + 0.44 \times \text{FTA})}\]

Below is every 25,000+ point scorer in NBA history, plotting Points Per Game (PPG) against True Shooting Percentage (TS%), with bubble size showing career Assists. LeBron averages 27+ PPG on nearly 59% True Shooting — more efficient than Michael Jordan (56.9%), Kobe Bryant (55.0%), Wilt Chamberlain (54.7%), and Tim Duncan (55.1%) — while simultaneously acting as his team’s primary point guard.

Ricardo Corvil • New College of Florida
